studies.Title: The relationship of serum dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate to subsequent cancer of the prostate.
studies.Reference: The relationship of serum dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate to subsequent cancer of the prostate.
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.Timing: Serum collected in 1974 before prostate cancer diagnosis during the following 12 years
studies.comparison_type: Prostate cancer cases versus age- and race-matched controls

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Levels of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) in sera collected and frozen in 1974 were studied among 81 prostate cancer cases diagnosed in the following 12 years and 81 age- and race-matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Levels of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) in sera collected and frozen in 1974 were studied among 81 prostate cancer cases diagnosed in the following 12 years and 81 age- and race-matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Although mean levels of DHEA were 11% lower among cases than controls and DHEA-S levels were 12% lower than among controls, no dose-response association was noted for either DHEA or DHEA-S.
extraction_supporting_text.design: 81 prostate cancer cases diagnosed in the following 12 years and 81 age- and race-matched controls
extraction_supporting_text.timing: sera collected and frozen in 1974 were studied among 81 prostate cancer cases diagnosed in the following 12 years
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Levels of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) in sera collected and frozen in 1974

studies.Title: V89L polymorphism of the 5alpha-reductase Type II gene (SRD5A2), endogenous sex hormones, and prostate cancer risk.
studies.Reference: V89L polymorphism of the 5alpha-reductase Type II gene (SRD5A2), endogenous sex hormones, and prostate cancer risk.
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

extraction_supporting_text.comparison: A moderate increase in risk associated with above-median serum levels of androstenedione and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) was present irrespective of V89L genotype.
extraction_supporting_text.design: in a case-control study (300 cases and 300 controls) nested within the Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: above-median serum levels of androstenedione and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS)
